milestones.title: M0 — Foundation
milestones.description: Core Android/QEMU, artifact, evidence, and repository foundations.

milestones.title: M0.5 — Public project surface
milestones.description: Issue-roadmap and agent foundations followed by the public static website.

milestones.title: M1 — Validated MVP
milestones.description: Complete one-phone Android, Linux guest, network, recovery, and durability path.

milestones.title: M2 — Early access
milestones.description: Release compliance, guided setup, verified downloads, device records, guides, and community testing.

milestones.title: M3 — Reliability
milestones.description: Thermal, storage, network, OEM lifecycle, upgrade, and device-class qualification.

milestones.title: M4 — Platform expansion
milestones.description: Stronger isolation, authentication, reproducible builds, controllers, Linux hosts, profiles, and runtime adapters.

milestones.title: MVP+ — USB physical link
milestones.description: Android Open Accessory link, QEMU stream NIC, Linux TAP/NAT, fallback, and optional artifact transfer.

items.title: Canonical VM profiles and artifact manifests
items.summary: Use one strict checked-in profile and artifact contract in production, labs, and tests.
items.outcome: Android, packaging, laboratories, and tests consume the same validated profile and active-manifest contracts.
items.whyNow: A shared source of truth prevents qualification from proving a configuration different from the APK.
nonGoals: No arbitrary profile execution or remote profile trust.
validation: Canonical package/profile and artifact-manifest checks pass.

items.title: Authenticated resumable artifact delivery
items.summary: Let a trusted controller deliver large verified artifacts without relying on a public server.
items.outcome: The Host API supports bounded authenticated resumable upload with digest verification and atomic publication.
items.whyNow: Remote deployment requires a private artifact path that does not weaken the public importer.
nonGoals: No general host file access or arbitrary URL fetch.
validation: Upload, replay, cancellation, digest, and manifest tests pass.

items.title: Evidence-bound hardware-in-the-loop runner
items.summary: Run one authoritative physical-device scenario path and bind evidence to an exact device, commit, and APK.
items.outcome: tests/hil owns the physical scenarios and produces bounded redacted evidence for the exact candidate.
items.whyNow: Physical claims must not be inferred from host, emulator, or package tests.
nonGoals: No device farm or automatic device selection.
validation: HIL unit tests and evidence promotion checks pass.

items.title: Deterministic Podroid vendoring and upstream sync
items.summary: Make inherited Podroid source and downstream patches reviewable, reproducible, and updateable.
items.outcome: The pinned subtree, ordered patch queue, external integration seam, and release provenance reproduce deterministically.
items.whyNow: The MVP depends on Podroid's APK-native QEMU behavior and must preserve upstream provenance.
nonGoals: No project-owned native rebuild claim yet.
validation: Offline reconstruction and release-provenance workflows pass.

items.title: Explicit phase and alpha compatibility policy
items.summary: Keep one authorised phase and prefer clean unreleased-alpha contracts over unneeded compatibility code.
items.outcome: Task tooling enforces phase packets, path ownership, context bounds, and explicit compatibility policy.
items.whyNow: Agents need safe autonomy without preserving obsolete development state as permanent complexity.
nonGoals: No migration framework without a real deployed population.
validation: Task, context, and scope validators pass.

items.title: Agent-safe supervised device validation
items.summary: Add serial leases, expiring scenario authorization, evidence classes, clean-tree promotion, and exact-input records.
items.outcome: Supervised physical work is bounded, attributable, non-destructive by default, and safe for agent participation.
items.whyNow: The one-phone MVP path needs clear human authorization before destructive or isolating actions.
nonGoals: No physical gate closes from harness code alone.
validation: PR #20 review, HIL unit tests, and full repository CI.

items.title: Establish public-site and issue-roadmap governance
items.summary: Define the static site, design system, theme, roadmap truth, Podroid-MVP alignment, and replanning contracts.
items.outcome: Accepted documentation separates durable direction, roadmap state, task authorization, acceptance evidence, and publication caches.
items.whyNow: Implementation needs one reviewed contract before the site or live roadmap exists.
nonGoals: No website source or product behavior.
validation: PR #19 merged with green CI and review closure.

items.title: Generate the GitHub issue roadmap and compact agent index
items.summary: Turn roadmap-labelled issues, milestones, and dependencies into a static public roadmap and bounded agent context.
items.outcome: A validated live issue graph produces a last-known-good public snapshot, compact agent index, and bounded per-issue context.
items.whyNow: Agents and the website must consume one roadmap rather than maintain separate plans.
nonGoals: No website pages, Android code, or acceptance changes.
validation: Seed, live bootstrap, dependency, snapshot, context, freshness, and idempotency tests pass.

items.title: Build the Astro design-system foundation
items.summary: Create a static component shell with one token-driven CSS system and accessible System, Light, and Dark theme control.
items.outcome: Astro builds static pages from reusable layout and design components in both themes with a no-JavaScript baseline.
items.whyNow: The public pages need a coherent accessible foundation before content is repeated across templates.
nonGoals: No browser-side GitHub calls or production release claims.
validation: Static build, theme, component-gallery, no-JS, accessibility, and link checks pass.

items.title: Publish the user-facing SalvageNet pages
items.summary: Publish simple, uplifting, honest pages for users and community members from shared components.
items.outcome: All agreed public pages render complete content with shared navigation, sections, safety language, and calls to action.
items.whyNow: People need an understandable project surface before early device testing expands.
nonGoals: No dedicated developer portal or unsupported compatibility claims.
validation: Content, links, responsive layout, accessibility, and no-JS checks pass.

items.title: Generate public acceptance and release status
items.summary: Keep public status current without hard-coded gate counts, candidate identities, or issue-derived validation claims.
items.outcome: Build-time generators project acceptance, evidence, release, and roadmap truth into bounded website data.
items.whyNow: Project status changes frequently and must remain evidence-aligned.
nonGoals: Issue closure never changes acceptance status.
validation: Generated data matches ledger/evidence and contains source provenance.

items.title: Add progressive-enhancement site components
items.summary: Add useful optional interactions while keeping every page complete without JavaScript.
items.outcome: Roadmap filters, search, checklist, checksum verification, evidence drawers, and restrained motion enhance static HTML.
items.whyNow: Small local interactions make a static site feel responsive without adding a server or account system.
nonGoals: No required JavaScript, remote analytics, or browser GitHub API.
validation: Keyboard, touch, focus, reduced-motion, local-only, and no-JS tests pass.

items.title: Deploy exact static artifacts with freshness evidence
items.summary: Publish the exact validated site artifact and expose when project data was last synchronized.
items.outcome: GitHub Actions builds, validates, archives, and deploys one exact static artifact with source hashes and stale-data protection.
items.whyNow: Independent provider rebuilds could publish data or dependencies different from the reviewed result.
nonGoals: No application server or silent stale roadmap publication.
validation: Exact-artifact CI, provenance, stale fallback, and deployment checks pass.

items.title: Qualify deterministic Ubuntu ARM64 guest boot
items.summary: Prove UEFI, QMP, NoCloud, key-only loopback SSH, restart, and secret hygiene before adding guest mesh.
items.outcome: One bounded host-QEMU run qualifies the canonical Ubuntu profile and exact artifacts without claiming Android behavior.
items.whyNow: Boot and mesh are separate failure domains; proving boot first makes phone debugging tractable.
nonGoals: No Headscale, Tailscale, emulator, or physical gate claim.
validation: H02A packet checks and reviewed host-QEMU evidence pass.

items.title: Qualify the guest private-network path
items.summary: Prove one-use guest enrolment, separate identity, tailnet SSH, restart, interruption, and recovery.
items.outcome: The Linux guest joins Headscale independently and remains recoverable through the Android-host boundary.
items.whyNow: Guest networking must be qualified separately before the complete phone vertical slice.
nonGoals: No Android or physical acceptance claim.
validation: One-use enrollment, tailnet SSH, restart, interruption, recovery, and residue checks pass.

items.title: Validate APK-native QEMU, host mesh, and Host API on Android
items.summary: Prove the device substrate on one exact ARM64 Android phone and APK.
items.outcome: The APK starts the known guest, the Android host joins Headscale, and the authenticated Host API is reachable.
items.whyNow: This is the first authoritative proof that the Podroid-derived process model works in the target environment.
nonGoals: No broad device compatibility claim.
validation: Exact-device HIL smoke and host-mesh/API evidence pass.

items.title: Validate remote Ubuntu deployment and ordinary guest SSH
items.summary: Deploy Ubuntu through the real controller path and reach the separately enrolled guest with ordinary SSH.
items.outcome: The controller delivers exact artifacts, applies one VM generation, and reaches the guest through its own identity.
items.whyNow: Remote provisioning is the central user path after the device substrate works.
nonGoals: No workload scheduler or cluster join inside the Host API.
validation: Controller upload/import, generation apply, guest identity, and ordinary SSH evidence pass.

items.title: Validate recovery SSH with guest mesh unavailable
items.summary: Prove that the Android host can recover a guest whose private guest network is broken.
items.outcome: An authorized controller reaches loopback-only guest SSH through the host while guest mesh is disabled.
items.whyNow: Recovery independence is a permanent product contract, not an optional support feature.
nonGoals: No unrestricted TCP forwarding.
validation: Guest mesh is disabled and bounded host-mediated SSH still succeeds.

items.title: Validate lifecycle, reboot, and controller-offline durability
items.summary: Prove that UI, service, process, reboot, and controller outages do not redefine desired VM state.
items.outcome: The host reconciles one VM without duplicates after lifecycle disruption and continues when the controller is absent.
items.whyNow: A node is useful only if the controller is not a runtime lease and UI lifetime does not own the VM.
nonGoals: No pre-unlock unattended guarantee on stock Android.
validation: Activity, service, process, reboot-after-unlock, and actual controller-offline evidence pass.

items.title: Seal one exact validated MVP candidate
items.summary: Bind every base acceptance result to one source commit, one APK, one device record, and reviewed evidence.
items.outcome: All B01–B20 gates pass against the same exact candidate and the repository publishes the evidence set.
items.whyNow: A collection of passes from different builds is not a validated MVP.
nonGoals: No USB or broad stable-release claim.
validation: Every base gate and final CI pass against one exact source/APK identity.

items.title: Publish release licensing and corresponding source
items.summary: Resolve repository licensing, notices, modification records, corresponding source, and exact binary/source identity before public APK distribution.
items.outcome: A public APK is accompanied by a reviewed compatible license position, notices, modifications, and corresponding source.
items.whyNow: Podroid is GPLv2 and public binary distribution requires clear compliance.
nonGoals: No legal conclusion without reviewed source and distribution facts.
validation: License, notice, source, modification, and exact-binary review passes before download publication.

items.title: Create guided early-access onboarding
items.summary: Help careful testers understand safety, trust, permissions, profiles, progress, recovery, and current limits.
items.outcome: The Android setup path gives a clear guided route from safe device preparation to first SSH and recovery checks.
items.whyNow: Early testers should not need internal architecture knowledge to avoid common mistakes.
nonGoals: No promise of unattended or universal device support.
validation: Guided setup, permission, error, recovery, and accessibility tests pass.

items.title: Publish first verified device compatibility records
items.summary: Turn physical evidence into clear model-specific compatibility records.
items.outcome: Named devices have public records tied to Android version, exact build, profile, duration, thermal notes, and limitations.
items.whyNow: Compatibility should be earned by evidence rather than model-name inference.
nonGoals: No family-wide claim from one device.
validation: Each published record links exact reviewed evidence and limitations.

items.title: Publish exact candidate downloads and verification
items.summary: Give testers one clear place to find a compliant exact candidate and verify it locally.
items.outcome: The downloads page binds APK checksum, signing identity, source commit, validation state, license/source material, and limitations.
items.whyNow: A public test build must be verifiable and must not imply stable production readiness.
nonGoals: No app-store or stable-release claim.
validation: Exact artifact, signature, checksum, source, evidence, and license/source links agree.

items.title: Publish tested user guides and recovery paths
items.summary: Publish versioned guides for installation, enrolment, deployment, SSH, recovery, reset, diagnostics, and removal.
items.outcome: Each guide names the tested build/environment and clearly separates tested, draft, and planned steps.
items.whyNow: Safe adoption depends on repeatable instructions and an understandable recovery path.
nonGoals: No developer API portal in the user-facing section.
validation: Guide procedures are rerun against the named build and pass link/accessibility checks.

items.title: Create a community device-test day process
items.summary: Let repair cafés, schools, libraries, and hackerspaces contribute safe comparable evidence.
items.outcome: A kit covers consent, battery inspection, setup, evidence, redaction, result labels, and follow-up.
items.whyNow: Community testing should produce useful records without pressuring owners or weakening safety.
nonGoals: No unsupervised device farm or invented community activity.
validation: A pilot test day completes safely and produces repeatable redacted records.

items.title: Improve diagnostics and support UX
items.summary: Make failures understandable without exposing credentials or guest data.
items.outcome: Users can see bounded operation state, likely failure layer, recovery action, and safe diagnostic export.
items.whyNow: The first community testers need useful support without a remote shell or secret-heavy logs.
nonGoals: No guest user-data collection or live credential export.
validation: Redaction, error-state, accessibility, and recovery guidance tests pass.

items.title: Qualify sustained thermal and power behavior
items.summary: Measure safe sustained operation instead of inferring it from a successful boot.
items.outcome: Defined workload classes have duration, charging, temperature, throttling, and stop-policy evidence.
items.whyNow: A phone that boots may still be unsuitable for sustained unattended work.
nonGoals: No universal energy-saving claim.
validation: Repeatable measured thermal/power runs and safety stop rules are reviewed.

items.title: Qualify storage pressure, export, reset, and uninstall behavior
items.summary: Make storage ownership, full-disk failure, data export, reset, and uninstall consequences explicit.
items.outcome: System/data boundaries and failure behavior remain understandable under storage pressure and removal.
items.whyNow: Early users need to know what persists, what is deleted, and how to recover data.
nonGoals: No backup-product claim.
validation: Pressure, reset, export, update, and uninstall scenarios pass with documented outcomes.

items.title: Qualify network transitions and coordination interruption
items.summary: Measure host and guest behavior across Wi-Fi changes, relay paths, and temporary Headscale interruption.
items.outcome: Published reliability facts describe reconnection, direct/relayed paths, MTU behavior, and coordination outages.
items.whyNow: A mobile-derived host sees network changes that a fixed server may not.
nonGoals: No promise that coordination is never needed.
validation: Controlled network-transition and coordination-interruption scenarios pass.

items.title: Qualify Android and OEM lifecycle behavior
items.summary: Expand beyond one phone without treating manufacturer background behavior as uniform.
items.outcome: Selected Android versions and OEM devices have comparable lifecycle and restart evidence.
items.whyNow: Stock Android policies and manufacturer behavior materially affect long-running nodes.
nonGoals: No broad compatibility claim from emulator-only testing.
validation: Named-device lifecycle matrix and evidence pass reviewed procedures.

items.title: Add measured resource admission and device classes
items.summary: Prevent obviously unsafe or unrealistic VM requests and communicate appropriate device roles.
items.outcome: Measured memory, storage, battery, and thermal facts drive admission warnings and reliability classes.
items.whyNow: Valid typed requests can still overcommit old hardware without device-aware policy.
nonGoals: No opaque score or unsupported automatic performance guarantee.
validation: Admission decisions are deterministic and trace to measured device facts.

items.title: Qualify app upgrade, rollback, and runtime continuity
items.summary: Make updates predictable for installed nodes.
items.outcome: Supported upgrade and rollback paths preserve or explicitly transform runtime state and data.
items.whyNow: An early-access node needs a recoverable update story before wider use.
nonGoals: No permanent alpha migration compatibility without real installed users.
validation: Exact-version upgrade, rollback, interrupted update, and data continuity scenarios pass.

items.title: Isolate QEMU from host controller credentials
items.summary: Reduce the impact of a hostile guest escaping QEMU and define the arbitrary-image threat boundary.
items.outcome: A proven process, UID, or engine-app boundary keeps controller credentials outside the QEMU trust zone.
items.whyNow: QEMU shares the app UID in the MVP, so arbitrary hostile images are out of scope.
nonGoals: No hostile-image claim before measured isolation.
validation: Threat model, exploit-boundary tests, credential isolation, and recovery pass.

items.title: Build project-owned native runtime artifacts from source
items.summary: Replace pinned release extraction with reproducible project-controlled builds and provenance.
items.outcome: QEMU, launcher, libslirp, kernel, initramfs, and qualification artifacts build from pinned source and patch queues.
items.whyNow: The pinned extraction path is deterministic but not a project-owned native build.
nonGoals: No silent replacement of the proven Podroid launch model.
validation: Reproducible source builds, provenance, packaging, signature, and device tests pass.

items.title: Create a durable Rust and Slint controller
items.summary: Replace the Python test client with a maintainable cross-platform controller and friendly UI.
items.outcome: A Rust controller core and Slint application implement the stable Host API without changing node contracts.
items.whyNow: The Python CLI is intentionally temporary and the durable controller should serve desktop and later mobile use.
nonGoals: No Android-host rewrite or workload orchestration model.
validation: Contract, enrollment, lifecycle, recovery, accessibility, and packaging tests pass.

items.title: Create Linux, SBC, and WSL host service
items.summary: Bring the same Host API and lifecycle semantics to stable computers.
items.outcome: A Rust service implements the host contracts with native Linux adapters and simple installation.
items.whyNow: The long-term platform includes stable hosts while preserving shared protocol and operation semantics.
nonGoals: No shared mutable Android implementation or premature daemon root.
validation: Host API conformance, lifecycle, install, upgrade, and controller tests pass.

items.title: Separate guest classes, images, sources, and family adapters
items.summary: Model boot contract, immutable image identity, artifact source, and distro-family bootstrap adapter independently without exposing raw host configuration.
items.outcome: Concrete guest families prove typed compatibility while desired state remains immutable and distribution sources remain replaceable.
items.whyNow: Supporting more than Alpine should not create a backend per distribution or allow invalid low-level combinations.
nonGoals: No arbitrary container-to-VM conversion or OCI-in-APK before evidence.
validation: At least two concrete families prove class/image/source separation and rollback semantics.

items.title: Qualify more guest profiles and a real K3s worker
items.summary: Expand qualified Linux choices and prove an externally managed cluster-worker path.
items.outcome: Representative ARM64 families pass the same contracts and a K3s worker joins, drains, leaves, and recovers under an external control plane.
items.whyNow: The base lab only checks K3s prerequisites and does not prove a real worker lifecycle.
nonGoals: No Kubernetes control plane or scheduler inside the Android Host API.
validation: Family contracts and worker join/drain/leave/recovery evidence pass.

items.title: Add a structurally different second mesh adapter
items.summary: Use Nebula or another provider to prove the host-mesh port is not merely Tailscale-shaped.
items.outcome: A second implementation satisfies the host-mesh state/address/recovery contracts without leaking provider models inward.
items.whyNow: One implementation cannot prove that the port is genuinely provider-neutral.
nonGoals: No provider abstraction rewrite before a concrete second implementation.
validation: Contract, Android lifecycle, recovery, and transition tests pass for the second adapter.

items.title: Add production artifact trust and OCI distribution
items.summary: Use TUF and digest-addressed OCI or HTTP transport for normalized bootable artifact distribution.
items.outcome: Signed metadata, rollback protection, digest identity, retention, and revocation protect public artifact channels.
items.whyNow: Digest and size alone are an MVP shortcut that expires before public executable/profile updates.
nonGoals: No arbitrary OCI application-container boot in Android.
validation: TUF/OCI publication, rollback, revocation, offline cache, and exact-digest tests pass.

items.title: Support more than one active VM
items.summary: Expand beyond the explicit one-VM MVP only after resource and lifecycle evidence supports it.
items.outcome: Multiple instances have isolated paths, disks, identities, operations, recovery, and measured admission.
items.whyNow: The domain keeps a future-compatible instance ID, but the MVP intentionally limits active instances.
nonGoals: No multiple-VM work while base gates or admission evidence remain incomplete.
validation: Isolation, concurrency, lifecycle, storage, networking, admission, and recovery tests pass.

items.title: Add reviewed multi-controller authentication
items.summary: Replace the MVP controller capability with reviewed mTLS or principal authorization, revocation, and recovery.
items.outcome: Bounded principals support multiple controllers, revocation, recovery, and audit without changing Host API resources.
items.whyNow: The imported high-entropy capability is a replaceable MVP adapter, not the production multi-admin model.
nonGoals: No arbitrary LAN exposure or identity model coupled to one mesh provider.
validation: Principal, mTLS, revocation, recovery, audit, and downgrade tests pass.

items.title: Publish Docker and Swarm reference provisioning
items.summary: Prove join, drain, leave, replacement, and recovery without moving orchestrator state into the Host API.
items.outcome: Ordinary guest provisioning tools manage a replaceable phone worker through documented resource envelopes and recovery.
items.whyNow: Reference recipes demonstrate interoperability while preserving the host-enablement boundary.
nonGoals: No Compose, Swarm, or cluster objects in the Host API.
validation: Join, drain, leave, replace, outage, and recovery recipes pass on qualified devices.

items.title: Create managed and patched Android reliability tiers
items.summary: Use Device Owner and narrowly patched Android capabilities without creating a general-purpose root shell.
items.outcome: Managed deployment tiers publish explicit policy, unattended behavior, update, and recovery guarantees.
items.whyNow: Stock Android first-unlock and OEM limits may justify stronger optional reliability tiers after the base path is proven.
nonGoals: No general root shell or hidden downgrade of stock-device support.
validation: Provisioning, policy, reboot, update, rollback, revocation, and recovery tests pass per tier.

items.title: Add an AVF runtime backend
items.summary: Implement AVF behind the existing runtime contract and compare it with QEMU on supported devices.
items.outcome: AVF satisfies the same desired-state, lifecycle, profile, diagnostics, and recovery contracts where available.
items.whyNow: A second runtime can be evaluated only after the QEMU contract and device behavior are measured.
nonGoals: No replacement of the proven QEMU path without comparative evidence.
validation: Contract conformance and device comparisons cover capability, performance, lifecycle, and recovery.

items.title: Create a delegated remote profile repository
items.summary: Support signed profile publication with controlled delegation and reviewed maintainer boundaries.
items.outcome: Remote profiles are signed, versioned, revocable, bounded, and delegated through explicit trust policy.
items.whyNow: The three checked-in trusted profiles are an MVP shortcut that expires before third-party publication.
nonGoals: No remote executable scripts outside reviewed profile trust boundaries.
validation: Signing, delegation, rollback, revocation, schema, and malicious-profile tests pass.

items.title: Add a web UI through a local controller bridge
items.summary: Keep keys, SSH, tunnels, and native tools outside the browser while offering a local web interface.
items.outcome: A browser controls the local native controller through a narrow loopback bridge without receiving private keys or raw tunnels.
items.whyNow: A web interface may improve accessibility after the durable controller exists, but browser security limits remain explicit.
nonGoals: No direct browser possession of SSH keys, mesh credentials, or arbitrary host shell.
validation: Loopback origin, CSRF, capability, key-boundary, accessibility, and recovery tests pass.

items.title: Establish Android Open Accessory control link
items.summary: Create a bounded reconnectable USB control channel between a Linux host and the Android app.
items.outcome: Linux and Android negotiate a versioned AOA control stream with bounded framing and reconnect state.
items.whyNow: This optional underlay begins only after all base acceptance gates pass.
nonGoals: No USB work before B01–B20 are all PASS.
validation: AOA attach, authorization, framing, disconnect, reconnect, and bounded-failure tests pass.

items.title: Attach a QEMU stream NIC through USB
items.summary: Carry framed Ethernet traffic from the Android USB bridge to a second QEMU guest NIC.
items.outcome: The guest receives eth1 through a typed QEMU stream-netdev path while SLIRP remains available.
items.whyNow: The USB underlay is useful only when it reaches the VM without replacing the fallback path.
nonGoals: No raw remote QEMU arguments or removal of SLIRP.
validation: NIC attach, traffic, MTU, disconnect, and QEMU lifecycle tests pass.

items.title: Provide Linux TAP and NAT internet through node-linkd
items.summary: Let a Linux or SBC host route the USB guest link to its network.
items.outcome: node-linkd creates bounded TAP/NAT connectivity, reports health, and cleans up host state.
items.whyNow: A simple Linux/SBC service is the optional internet provider for the USB guest link.
nonGoals: No permanent privileged daemon before the base MVP and explicit authorization.
validation: TAP, NAT, DNS, cleanup, reconnect, and least-privilege tests pass.

items.title: Fail safely between USB and SLIRP
items.summary: Keep guest connectivity understandable when the optional USB link appears or disappears.
items.outcome: Routing prefers a healthy USB path and returns to SLIRP without losing host recovery.
items.whyNow: An optional cable must not make the ordinary fallback or recovery less reliable.
nonGoals: No silent route flapping or dependence on USB for recovery.
validation: Attach, health, preference, disconnect, fallback, reconnect, and recovery tests pass.

items.title: Harden USB and add optional artifact transfer
items.summary: Version and bound the USB protocol, improve diagnostics, and optionally transfer artifacts without weakening fallback.
items.outcome: The reviewed protocol supports negotiation, diagnostics, bounded artifact transfer, and security hardening.
items.whyNow: Artifact transfer is a later optimization after the network path and production artifact trust exist.
nonGoals: No weakening of digest verification, network fallback, or controller authorization.
validation: Version negotiation, bounds, integrity, interruption, replay, diagnostics, and fallback tests pass.
